I will keep my land mainly in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most dependable way for me to use the full year, match our water and temperature conditions, and keep grain output steady. I would rather choose stable, familiar grain crops than chase something riskier, because at the start of the season my first concern is securing yield and controlling costs. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put more attention on base fertilizer and a few key irrigations, and keep pesticide sprays limited to the periods when disease or aphids usually matter. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly with hybrid seed, use a little more nitrogen because maize responds well to it, and focus on timely watering, weed control, and one or two pest treatments if pressure shows up. I will use rotary tillage for wheat establishment after maize, and for summer maize I will keep the turnaround fast with no-tillage direct seeding after wheat so I do not lose soil moisture or planting time.
